newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail half-year net profit up 28 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail half-year net profit up 28 pct.

text.p: Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd on Tuesday announced a net profit of NZ$24.1 million for the six months to December 31, up $5.2 million on the $18.9 million posted in the comparable six month period a year ago.
"The increase in net profit reflects reduced interest costs and increased traffic levels," Tranz Rail said in a statement.
Earnings per share fell to 19 cents compared with 20 cents for the same period in the previous year.
Tranz Rail said the reduction in earnings per share reflected the higher level of ordinary shares issued, which increased 35 percent as a result of the June 1996 global initial public offering.
The company said its results had continued to improve while the New Zealand economy showed modest growth.
Revenue from rail and maritime operations for the first half of the 1997 financial year was $275.5 million, up three percent on the half year ended December 31, 1995.
Revenue tonne kilometres for freight traffic increased seven percent over the prior year's operation.
Passenger growth on Tranz Rail's Interisland services grew seven percent while rail passenger ridership rose five percent.
Total operating costs for the first half increased two percent to $238.2 million.

Operating profit for the half year increased slightly to $46.6 million from $46.4 million in the previous comparable period, reflecting an operating ratio of 83.7 percent versus 83.5 percent a year ago.

Net interest expense and deferred financing cost amortisation decreased to $10.2 million for the six months from $17.5 million previously as a result of repayment of long term debt following the company's public offering.
Included in the 1997 six month period was a one-time pre-tax charge of $1.4 million related to the repayment of the company's bank debt following the December 1996 sale and leaseback transaction.
Taxation expense increased to $12.3 million from $10.0 million in the previous six month period.
